title: Los Angeles pianists and Hampton Hawes
summary: Brown asks about Hampton Hawes and other pianists on the scene.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: If you are recounting when you were in Los Angeles in the late ’50s, ’58, there were other pianists there. Hampton Hawes. Did you get a chance to . . . ?
And Curtis Counce. Do you remember him? Curtis Counce?
Yeah. Curtis Counce was a bass player.
Yeah, right. But I’m thinking of . . .
Art Hillary. I’m trying to think of another one. Who else?
I think Jimmy Bond was there.
But how about Hampton Hawes? How . . . ?

Yeah, I dug Hamp. Hamp was – I saw Hamp in a club in Hollywood. He had some of those problems. He didn’t say much of anything. He would just say, “We’re going to play a song by Charlie Parker.” And then he’d play. Next song, we’re going to play whatever, and just kept playing.
